questions.question: Three partners A, B, and C started a business. A invested Rs. 30,000, B invested Rs. 20,000, and C invested Rs. 25,000. After 6 months, A withdrew Rs. 5,000 and C invested Rs. 7,000 more. At the end of the year, the firm incurred a loss of Rs. 24,000. Find the share of loss borne by partner C.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of loss **A : B : C** = (30 × 6 + 25 × 6) : (20 × 12) : (25 × 6 + 32 × 6)

Ratio = 330 : 240 : 342 ⇒ **55 : 40 : 57**

Total units = 55 + 40 + 57 = 152 units

**C's loss share** = (57 ÷ 152) × 24,000 = 3 × 3,000 = 9,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial **investments** of **A**, **B**, and **C** are ₹30,000, ₹20,000, and ₹25,000 respectively.

After **6 months**, **A** withdrew ₹5,000 and **C** invested ₹7,000 more. The total **loss** is ₹24,000.

**Formula Used:**

**Profit or Loss Share Ratio** = (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂) : (Capital₃ × Time₃)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/231dfb04b14823880d03c543799def1254ecb3337ae4035a9b3eb00ad1fac277.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total investment units for **A** = (30,000 × 6) + (25,000 × 6) = 1,80,000 + 1,50,000 = 3,30,000

⇒ Total investment units for **B** = 20,000 × 12 = 2,40,000

⇒ Total investment units for **C** = (25,000 × 6) + (32,000 × 6) = 1,50,000 + 1,92,000 = 3,42,000

⇒ **Ratio A : B : C** = 3,30,000 : 2,40,000 : 3,42,000

⇒ Simplifying the ratio (dividing by 6,000) = **55 : 40 : 57**

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 55 + 40 + 57 = 152 units

⇒ **Loss share of C** = (57 ÷ 152) × 24,000

⇒ **Loss share of C** = 57 × (24,000 ÷ 152) = 57 × (3,000 ÷ 19)

⇒ **Loss share of C** = 3 × 3,000 = 9,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹9,000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership Ratio Principle

The profit or loss is always distributed in the ratio of the product of **Capital** and **Time**. If the time period is different for different investments by the same person, use the weighted average sum.

Active vs Sleeping Partner

An **active partner** manages the business and may receive a salary or extra commission before the remaining profit is divided, whereas a **sleeping partner** only provides capital.

Loss Distribution

Just like profits, **losses** are also borne in the same ratio of **Investment × Time** unless a specific contract states otherwise.

questions.question: A tank contains 120 litres of liquid, 30% of which is alcohol. If 30 litres of this mixture is replaced by another liquid containing 50% alcohol, what is the percentage of alcohol in the resulting solution?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **remaining liquid** (90 L) to **added liquid** (30 L) = 3 : 1

Alcohol concentration in remaining = 30%, in added = 50%

Net Alcohol % = [(3 × 30) + (1 × 50)] ÷ (3 + 1)

Net Alcohol % = 140 ÷ 4 = 35%

**∴ The correct answer is 35%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Volume = 120 L, Initial Alcohol = 30%

Replaced Volume = 30 L, Replacement Alcohol = 50%

**Formula Used:**

Final Alcohol % = (Total Alcohol Quantity ÷ Total Solution Volume) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a9747ffbd664dd3f174721d9b1de69082b8572953692f8865dfc1e1ab3e7eac2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Alcohol in **remaining 90 L** = 30% of 90 = (30/100) × 90 = 27 L

⇒ Alcohol in **added 30 L** = 50% of 30 = (50/100) × 30 = 15 L

⇒ **Total Alcohol** in final mixture = 27 + 15 = 42 L

⇒ **Total volume** of final mixture = 120 − 30 + 30 = 120 L

⇒ Resulting Alcohol % = (42 ÷ 120) × 100

⇒ Resulting Alcohol % = (7 ÷ 20) × 100 = 35%

**∴ The correct answer is 35%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Principle

When two mixtures of quantities Q₁ and Q₂ with concentrations C₁ and C₂ are mixed, the final concentration is (Q₁C₁ + Q₂C₂) ÷ (Q₁ + Q₂).

Alligation Rule

Ratio of quantities = (Higher Rate − Mean Rate) ÷ (Mean Rate − Lower Rate). This helps find the proportion in which two ingredients are mixed.

Replacement Concept

Removing 'x' litres from a mixture does not change the concentration of the remaining liquid; only the quantity reduces before adding the new liquid.</p

questions.question: The ratio of the speeds of two trains is 5 : 7. If the faster train travels 210 km in 3 hours, find the time taken by the slower train to cover 150 km.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Speed of the **faster train** = 210 ÷ 3 = 70 kmph.

According to the ratio 5 : 7, if 7 units = 70 kmph, then 1 unit = 10 kmph.

Speed of the **slower train** = 5 units = 5 × 10 = 50 kmph.

**Time taken** by slower train = 150 ÷ 50 = 3 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio of speeds = 5 : 7, Distance (Faster) = 210 km, Time (Faster) = 3 hr, Distance (Slower) = 150 km.

**Formula Used:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time; Time = Distance ÷ Speed

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c7a5e65f51290c112b278d8a28f9fc2a00e2c71837466c1392d74f346d9afd32.png] 

⇒ **Speed of Faster Train** = 210 ÷ 3 = 70 kmph

⇒ Speed of Slower Train / Speed of Faster Train = 5 / 7

⇒ Speed of Slower Train / 70 = 5 / 7

⇒ **Speed of Slower Train** = (5 × 70) ÷ 7 = 50 kmph

⇒ **Time taken** by Slower Train = 150 ÷ 50 = 3 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 3 hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relationship

When distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/hr to m/s, multiply by 5/18. To convert from m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Average Speed

Average speed = (Total Distance) ÷ (Total Time). For two equal distances with speeds x and y, Average Speed = 2xy/(x+y).</p

questions.question:
Arrange the following values in ascending order:
 2(3)/(8), (20)/(7), 2(1)/(2), (37)/(14)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Convert each value into **Decimal Form** for immediate comparison:

2(3/8) = 2 + 0.375 = 2.375

20/7 = 2.857...

2(1/2) = 2 + 0.5 = 2.5

37/14 = 2.642...

Comparing the values: 2.375 **__Alternate Method__**

**Given Values:** 2(3/8), 20/7, 2(1/2), 37/14

Convert **Mixed Fractions** to **Improper Fractions**:

⇒ 2(3/8) = (2 × 8 + 3) / 8 = 19/8

⇒ 2(1/2) = (2 × 2 + 1) / 2 = 5/2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/17ea177661b0b48ae4afa7fbb0197f6a60a6756dcf02ac889f3d3b96b24bbd57.png] 

To compare fractions, find the **LCM** of denominators 8, 7, 2, and 14.

⇒ **LCM**(8, 7, 2, 14) = 56

Express all fractions with denominator 56:

⇒ 19/8 = (19 × 7) / (8 × 7) = 133/56

⇒ 20/7 = (20 × 8) / (7 × 8) = 160/56

⇒ 5/2 = (5 × 28) / (2 × 28) = 140/56

⇒ 37/14 = (37 × 4) / (14 × 4) = 148/56

Comparing **Numerators**: 133 **__Additional Information__**

Comparing Like Fractions

When denominators are the same, the fraction with the **larger numerator** is greater.

Cross Multiplication Method

To compare a/b and c/d, compare the products (a × d) and (b × c). If ad > bc, then a c/d.

Decimal Conversion

Dividing the numerator by the denominator provides a decimal value, which is often the **fastest way** to rank multiple fractions.</p

questions.question: (1)/(8+sqrt{7)} + (1)/(8-sqrt{7)} = ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For fractions with **conjugate denominators** of the form (a + √b) and (a − √b), the sum 1/(a + √b) + 1/(a − √b) simplifies to 2a / (a² − b).

Here, a = 8 and b = 7.

Sum = (2 × 8) / (8² − 7) = 16 / (64 − 7) = 16/57.

**∴ The correct answer is 16/57.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 1/(8 + √7) + 1/(8 − √7)

**Formula Used:** Sum of fractions = (a/b) + (c/d) = (ad + bc) / bd

⇒ Sum = [1 × (8 − √7) + 1 × (8 + √7)] / [(8 + √7)(8 − √7)]

⇒ Sum = (8 − √7 + 8 + √7) / [8² − (√7)²]

⇒ Sum = 16 / (64 − 7)

⇒ Sum = 16/57

**∴ The correct answer is 16/57.**

**__Additional Information__**

Rationalization of Denominator

To eliminate a square root from the denominator, multiply both numerator and denominator by the **conjugate surd** (change the sign between the terms).

Difference of Squares

The algebraic identity (x + y)(x − y) = x² − y² is fundamental when simplifying expressions involving **square roots**.

Conjugate Surds Property

The product of two **conjugate surds** (a + √b) and (a − √b) is always a **rational number**, which is a² − b.</p

questions.question: frac{(sqrt{5} + sqrt{2})² + (sqrt{5} - sqrt{2})²}{6sqrt{10}} = ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the **algebraic identity**: (a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²).

Here, a = √5 and b = √2.

Numerator = 2((√5)² + (√2)²) = 2(5 + 2) = 14.

Expression = 14 / 6√10 = 7 / 3√10.

By **rationalizing**: (7 × √10) / (3√10 × √10) = 7√10/30.

**∴ The correct answer is 7√10/30.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** [(√5 + √2)² + (√5 − √2)²] / 6√10

**Formula Used:** (a + b)² = a² + b² + 2ab and (a − b)² = a² + b² − 2ab

Expanding the numerator:

⇒ (√5 + √2)² = (√5)² + (√2)² + 2(√5)(√2) = 5 + 2 + 2√10 = 7 + 2√10
⇒ (√5 − √2)² = (√5)² + (√2)² − 2(√5)(√2) = 5 + 2 − 2√10 = 7 − 2√10
⇒ Numerator = (7 + 2√10) + (7 − 2√10) = 14
⇒ Final Expression = 14 / 6√10
⇒ Value = 7 / 3√10

**Rationalizing the denominator:**

⇒ Value = (7 × √10) / (3√10 × √10)
⇒ Value = 7√10 / (3 × 10)
⇒ Value = 7√10 / 30

**∴ The correct answer is 7√10/30.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²) and (a + b)² − (a − b)² = 4ab.

Rationalization of Surds

To rationalize a denominator of the form √a, multiply both **numerator** and **denominator** by √a.

Product of Square Roots

For any positive real numbers x and y, √x × √y = √(xy).</p

questions.question: What is the remainder when 1349 is divided by 8?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **remainder** when a number is divided by **8**, we only need to check the **last three digits** of that number.

The **last three digits** of 1349 are **349**.

Dividing 349 by 8: 349 = (8 × 43) + **5**.

Since the last three digits leave a **remainder of 5**, the entire number 1349 also leaves a **remainder of 5** when divided by 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Dividend = 1349

Divisor = 8

**Formula Used:**

Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/29bdf1ccba077222a59c5dc05418f89ba2a55b7e6d3a27f017d4dd144d6dfa46.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Divide 1349 by 8 step-by-step:

⇒ 13 ÷ 8 = 1, **Remainder** = 5

⇒ Bring down 4, making it 54. 54 ÷ 8 = 6, **Remainder** = 6

⇒ Bring down 9, making it 69. 69 ÷ 8 = 8, **Remainder** = 5

⇒ 1349 = (8 × 168) + 5

⇒ **Final Remainder** = 5

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 2

A number is divisible by 2 if its **last digit** is even (0, 2, 4, 6, or 8).

Divisibility Rule of 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the **last two digits** are divisible by 4 (e.g., 1348 is divisible by 4 because 48 is).

General Rule for 2ⁿ

A number is divisible by 2ⁿ if the **last n digits** of that number are divisible by 2ⁿ.</p

questions.question: Which of the following number is neither divisible by 9 nor by 11?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the **sum of digits** for **divisibility by 9**: 3472 → 16 (No), 3168 → 18 (Yes), 3366 → 18 (Yes), 3465 → 18 (Yes).

Since 3168, 3366, and 3465 are all divisible by 9, they are excluded.

Now check 3472 for **divisibility by 11**: (4 + 2) − (3 + 7) = 6 − 10 = −4 (Not divisible by 11).

Thus, 3472 is **neither divisible by 9 nor by 11**.

**∴ The correct answer is 3472.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given numbers:** 3472, 3168, 3366, 3465

**Step 1: Check Divisibility by 9** (Sum of digits must be a multiple of 9)

⇒ For 3472: 3 + 4 + 7 + 2 = 16 (Not divisible by 9)

⇒ For 3168: 3 + 1 + 6 + 8 = 18 (Divisible by 9)

⇒ For 3366: 3 + 3 + 6 + 6 = 18 (Divisible by 9)

⇒ For 3465: 3 + 4 + 6 + 5 = 18 (Divisible by 9)

**Step 2: Check Divisibility by 11** (Difference of sum of digits at even and odd positions must be 0 or a multiple of 11)

⇒ For 3472: (4 + 2) − (3 + 7) = 6 − 10 = −4 (Not divisible by 11)

⇒ For 3168: (1 + 8) − (3 + 6) = 9 − 9 = 0 (Divisible by 11)

⇒ For 3366: (3 + 6) − (3 + 6) = 9 − 9 = 0 (Divisible by 11)

⇒ For 3465: (4 + 5) − (3 + 6) = 9 − 9 = 0 (Divisible by 11)

**Conclusion:** 3472 is the only number failing both conditions.

**∴ The correct answer is 3472.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 9. For example, 729 (7+2+9=18) is divisible by 9.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the **difference** between the sum of digits at **odd places** and the sum of digits at **even places** is either 0 or a multiple of 11.

LCM of 9 and 11

If a number is divisible by both 9 and 11, it must be divisible by their **LCM**, which is 9 × 11 = 99.</p

questions.question: The average of 10 numbers is X and one of these numbers is 70. If 70 is replaced with 30, then what will be the new average?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net change in the sum = **New value** − **Old value** = 30 − 70 = **−40**.

Change in the **average** = Total change ÷ Total numbers = −40 ÷ 10 = **−4**.

**New Average** = Old average + Change = X − 4.

**∴ The correct answer is X − 4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of terms = 10

Initial **Average** = X

Value replaced = 70

Replacement value = 30

**Formula Used:**

Total Sum = Average × Number of terms

New Average = New Sum ÷ Number of terms

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fc32460d402bd7ca7b26684a3c06d1e18f0fb0e03db91477d9933c69ca254f7a.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Sum** of 10 numbers = 10 × X = 10X

⇒ **New Sum** after replacement = 10X − 70 + 30

⇒ **New Sum** = 10X − 40

⇒ **New Average** = (10X − 40) ÷ 10

⇒ **New Average** = 10X/10 − 40/10 = X − 4

**∴ The correct answer is X − 4.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean Properties

If each observation in a data set is **increased** or **decreased** by a constant **k**, the **mean** of the data set also increases or decreases by **k**.

Net Deviation Rule

The algebraic sum of the **deviations** of a set of observations from their **arithmetic mean** is always **zero** (Σ(xᵢ − mean) = 0).

Weighted Average

When combining two groups with different averages, use **Avgw** = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + dots + 45³ = ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **sum of cubes** of the first **n natural numbers** is calculated as [n(n + 1) / 2]².

For **n = 45**, the sum is [45 × 46 / 2]².

⇒ [45 × 23]² = 1035².

⇒ 1035² = 1071225.

**∴ The correct answer is 1071225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The series is the sum of cubes of the first **45 natural numbers**: 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + ... + 45³.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of cubes of first **n** natural numbers (Sₙ) = [n(n + 1) / 2]²

**Calculations:**

⇒ Here, **n = 45**.

⇒ S₄₅ = [45 × (45 + 1) / 2]²

⇒ S₄₅ = [45 × 46 / 2]²

⇒ S₄₅ = [45 × 23]²

⇒ S₄₅ = 1035²

⇒ S₄₅ = (1000 + 35)²

⇒ S₄₅ = 1000² + 2 × 1000 × 35 + 35²

⇒ S₄₅ = 1000000 + 70000 + 1225

⇒ S₄₅ = 1071225

**∴ The correct answer is 1071225.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of the first n natural numbers is given by the formula: Sₙ = n(n + 1) / 2.

Sum of Squares of First n Natural Numbers

The sum of squares (1² + 2² + ... + n²) is given by: Sₙ = n(n + 1)(2n + 1) / 6.

Relationship between Sum and Cube Sum

The sum of cubes of the first n natural numbers is exactly equal to the **square of the sum** of the first n natural numbers.</p

questions.question: The average of 12 numbers is 46. Four numbers 20, 8, 12 and 40 were removed. What will be the new average?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Sum of **4 removed numbers** = 20 + 8 + 12 + 40 = 80

Average of removed numbers = 80 ÷ 4 = 20

**Deviation** from original average per number = 46 − 20 = 26

Total surplus distributed to remaining 8 numbers = 4 × 26 = 104

Increase in average = 104 ÷ 8 = 13

**New Average** = 46 + 13 = 59

**∴ The correct answer is 59.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of 12 numbers = 46; Numbers removed = 20, 8, 12, 40.

**Formula Used:** Sum = Average × Count; New Average = (Total Sum − Removed Sum) ÷ (Original Count − Removed Count)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a39fd6b2c564285c28520a92ed07d31aa815d7026c2facb802923bf153c921d.png] 

⇒ **Total sum** of 12 numbers = 12 × 46 = 552

⇒ Sum of 4 removed numbers = 20 + 8 + 12 + 40 = 80

⇒ **Remaining sum** = 552 − 80 = 472

⇒ Remaining count of numbers = 12 − 4 = 8

⇒ New average = 472 ÷ 8

⇒ **New average** = 59

**∴ The correct answer is 59.**

**__Additional Information__**

Average Concept

Average = Total Sum ÷ Number of observations. If the removed numbers are less than the average, the new average will increase.

Weighted Average

Combined average of two groups = (n₁ × A₁ + n₂ × A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the count and A is the average.

Net Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from the average is always zero. This is used for quick calculations when items are added or removed.</p

questions.question: B = 3560 - A. When B is divided by 8, 12 and 16 the remainder is 4 in each case. What is the value of A?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Find the **LCM** of the divisors: **LCM(8, 12, 16) = 48**.

The number **B** must be of the form **48k + 4**.

Find the multiple of 48 nearest to 3560: **48 × 74 = 3552**.

Thus, **B = 3552 + 4 = 3556**.

Substitute B in the equation: **A = 3560 − 3556 = 4**.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Equation: **B = 3560 − A**

⇒ Divisors: **8, 12, 16**; Remainder: **4**

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **Dividend = (LCM × Quotient) + Remainder**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/44246f4eda991fe1b0fc94ac4003621bdb4ac140de863931d39770a5a393085f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, calculate the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of 8, 12, and 16:

⇒ 8 = 2³

⇒ 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ 16 = 2⁴

⇒ **LCM = 2⁴ × 3 = 16 × 3 = 48**

⇒ Any number that leaves a remainder of 4 when divided by 8, 12, and 16 must be of the form: **B = 48k + 4**

⇒ Since **B = 3560 − A** and **A** is small, **B** is close to 3560.

⇒ Divide 3560 by 48 to find the nearest multiple: **3560 ÷ 48 = 74** with a remainder of **8**.

⇒ Multiple of 48 just below 3560: **48 × 74 = 3552**.

⇒ Therefore, **B = 3552 + 4 = 3556**.

⇒ From the given equation: **3556 = 3560 − A**

⇒ **A = 3560 − 3556 = 4**.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

**__Additional Information__**

LCM and Remainder Theorem

If a number N leaves the same remainder **r** when divided by **x, y, and z**, then **N = LCM(x, y, z) × k + r**, where k is an integer.

Divisibility Rule of 16

A number is divisible by **16** if the number formed by its **last four digits** is divisible by 16.

Relationship of Division

The fundamental relation is **Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder**, where the remainder is always less than the divisor.</p

questions.question: There is a rectangular floor of size 540 { cm} times 720 { cm} . The floor is to tiled with largest square tiles. How many such tiles will be required?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the **largest square tile**, calculate the **HCF** of the dimensions 540 cm and 720 cm.

**HCF**(540, 720) = 180 cm (This is the side of each square tile).

Number of tiles along length = 720 ÷ 180 = 4.

Number of tiles along breadth = 540 ÷ 180 = 3.

Total tiles required = 4 × 3 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Length** of the floor = 720 cm

**Breadth** of the floor = 540 cm

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2f632002ac8b6710d140a14a9843bada109bb81af22dc3ed8a251375f079100d.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Side of the largest square tile = **HCF**(Length, Breadth)

Number of tiles = (Area of floor) ÷ (Area of one square tile)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Side of square tile = HCF(540, 720)

⇒ 540 = 2² × 3³ × 5

⇒ 720 = 2⁴ × 3² × 5

⇒ HCF = 2² × 3² × 5 = 4 × 9 × 5 = 180 cm

⇒ Area of floor = 540 × 720 cm²

⇒ Area of one tile = 180 × 180 cm²

⇒ Number of tiles = (540 × 720) ÷ (180 × 180)

⇒ Number of tiles = (540 ÷ 180) × (720 ÷ 180)

⇒ Number of tiles = 3 × 4 = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

HCF is the largest positive integer that divides two or more integers without leaving a remainder. It is essential for problems involving **maximum size** or **equal distribution**.

Area and Tiling

The number of tiles required to cover an area is always calculated as **Total Area ÷ Area of one tile**, provided the dimensions are perfectly divisible by the tile size.

Square Area Formula

Area of a square = side × side (or s²). In this problem, s = HCF(Length, Breadth).</p

questions.question: 30 percent of a number exceeds 20 percent of the same number by 40. What is the value of the number?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Difference in **percentage** = 30% − 20% = 10%

This 10% difference is given as **40**.

Since 10% → 40

Then 100% (the **number**) → 40 × 10 = 400

**∴ The correct answer is 400.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First part = 30% of the number

Second part = 20% of the number

Difference = 40

**Formula Used:**

Percentage Value = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Total Value

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/55afada82b9268f15134101d22de81e6c55b914325e5ba7328b50b17b509848f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **number** be x.

⇒ 30% of x − 20% of x = 40

⇒ (30/100) × x − (20/100) × x = 40

⇒ (10/100) × x = 40

⇒ 0.1x = 40

⇒ x = 40 ÷ 0.1

⇒ x = 400

**∴ The correct answer is 400.**

**__Additional Information__**

Percentage Difference Rule

When comparing two percentages of the same base, the difference in their values is directly proportional to the difference in their percentage points.

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

To convert x% to a fraction, divide x by 100. For example, 10% = 10/100 = 1/10.

Base Value Concept

The 'number' in such problems is always considered the 100% base value from which other percentages are calculated.</p

questions.question: Every day a person sells 40\% of his fruits and 10\% of the remaining fruits get spoilt during the night. If total 36 fruits got spoil on the first night, then how many fruits did he sell on the first day?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Assume **total fruits** = 100 units.

**Fruits sold** = 40 units; **Remaining fruits** = 60 units.

**Spoilt fruits** = 10% of 60 = 6 units.

Given: 6 units = 36 fruits ⇒ 1 unit = 6 fruits.

**Sold fruits** = 40 units × 6 = 240 fruits.

**∴ The correct answer is 240 fruits.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Percentage of fruits sold** = 40%

**Percentage of remaining spoilt** = 10%

**Fruits spoilt** = 36

**Formula Used:**

Remaining fruits = Total − Sold

Spoilt fruits = Percentage × Remaining fruits

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa0c7f3ab865e58e08faea488a4891db3f2f39edb093e8db0bff6dbbd642b8cb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **total number of fruits** be x.

⇒ **Fruits sold** = 40% of x = 0.40x.

⇒ **Remaining fruits** = x − 0.40x = 0.60x.

⇒ **Fruits spoilt** = 10% of 0.60x = 0.10 × 0.60x = 0.06x.

⇒ Given: 0.06x = 36.

⇒ x = 36 ÷ 0.06 = 600.

⇒ **Fruits sold** = 0.40 × 600 = 240.

**∴ The correct answer is 240 fruits.**

**__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage

When a quantity is reduced by x% and the remainder is further reduced by y%, the final value is Total × (1 − x/100) × (1 − y/100).

Percentage Conversion

To find the original value from a percentage, use: (Given Value ÷ Percentage Value) × 100.</p

questions.question: R is 33.33 percent more efficient than S. S alone can finish a work in 24 days. In how many days will R alone finish the same work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency ratio **R : S** = 133.33% : 100% = 4 : 3.

Since **Work** is constant, the **Time ratio** is the inverse of **Efficiency** → **R : S** = 3 : 4.

Given **S** takes 24 days, so 4 units = 24 days ⇒ 1 unit = 6 days.

Time for **R** = 3 units = 3 × 6 = 18 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Efficiency of **R** is 33.33% (1/3) more than **S**.

Time taken by **S** alone = 24 days.

**Formula Used:**

**Total Work** = **Efficiency** × **Time Taken**

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 **S**
 24
 72 units
 3
 
 

 **R**
 18
 4
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the efficiency of **S** be 3 units/day.

⇒ Efficiency of **R** = 3 + (33.33% of 3) = 3 + 1 = 4 units/day.

⇒ **Total Work** = Efficiency of **S** × Days taken by **S** = 3 × 24 = 72 units.

⇒ Time taken by **R** = **Total Work** ÷ Efficiency of **R**

⇒ Time taken by **R** = 72 ÷ 4 = 18 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 18 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Variation in Work

When the amount of work is constant, the time required to complete the work is inversely proportional to the efficiency (E₁ × T₁ = E₂ × T₂).

Percentage to Fraction Conversion

Standard fractions like 33.33% = 1/3, 66.66% = 2/3, and 16.66% = 1/6 are frequently used in efficiency problems to simplify calculations.

Combined Work Formula

If **R** and **S** work together, their combined efficiency is ER + ES, and the time taken is Total Work ÷ (ER + ES).</p

questions.question: Pipes P1 and P2 alone can fill a tank in 5 hours and 10 hours respectively. Pipe P3 alone can empty the same tank in 20 hours. Firstly, both pipes P1 and P2 are opened and after 1 hour pipe P3 is also opened. In how much total time (in hours) tank will be completely filled?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total work (LCM of 5, 10, 20) = 20 units.

Efficiencies: **Pipe P1** = 4, **Pipe P2** = 2, **Pipe P3** = −1 (emptying).

Work in 1st hour by **P1** and **P2** = 4 + 2 = 6 units.

Remaining work = 20 − 6 = 14 units, to be filled at rate (4 + 2 − 1) = 5 units/hr.

Total time = 1 + 14/5 = 19/5 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 19/5 hr.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **P1** = 5 hr, **P2** = 10 hr, **P3** = 20 hr (empty).

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (hr)**
 **Total Work (units)**
 **Efficiency (units/hr)**
 
 

 P1 (Fill)
 5
 20
 4
 
 

 P2 (Fill)
 10
 2
 
 

 P3 (Empty)
 20
 −1
 
 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Total Capacity** of the tank = LCM(5, 10, 20) = 20 units.

⇒ Work done by **P1** and **P2** in the first 1 hour = (4 + 2) × 1 = 6 units.

⇒ Remaining capacity to be filled = 20 − 6 = 14 units.

⇒ After 1 hour, all three pipes are open, so **Combined Efficiency** = 4 + 2 − 1 = 5 units/hr.

⇒ Time required to fill the remaining tank = 14 ÷ 5 = 14/5 hr.

⇒ **Total Time** taken to fill the tank = 1 + 14/5 = 19/5 hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 19/5 hr.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inlet and Outlet Pipes

An inlet pipe fills the tank (positive efficiency), while an outlet pipe empties it (negative efficiency).

Net Efficiency

When multiple pipes work together, the net rate of work is the algebraic sum of their individual efficiencies.

Total Time Principle

If work is done in phases, the total time is the sum of the time durations of each individual phase.</p

questions.question: Speeds of train P and Q is 65 { m/s} and 50 { m/s} . Train P and Q are running in same direction. They cross each other in 50 seconds. What is total length (in metres) of trains P and Q?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** (Same direction) = 65 − 50 = 15 m/s

**Total Length** of trains = Relative Speed × Time

Total Length = 15 × 50 = 750 m

**∴ The correct answer is 750 m.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bef59d1c3a58c011201d54aae824793c35e4a42ea68b12bb493a289b42ca1979.png] 

**Given:**

Speed of **Train P** (SP) = 65 m/s

Speed of **Train Q** (SQ) = 50 m/s

**Time** taken to cross each other (T) = 50 sec

**Formula Used:**

When two objects move in the **same direction**, Relative Speed (Sᵣₑₗ) = SP − SQ

Distance (Total Length) = Relative Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 65 − 50

⇒ Relative Speed = 15 m/s

⇒ Total Length = Sᵣₑₗ × T

⇒ Total Length = 15 × 50

⇒ Total Length = 750 m

**∴ The correct answer is 750 m.**

**__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

If two trains move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (S₁ + S₂).

Crossing stationary objects

When a train crosses a **pole** or a tree, the distance covered is its own length. When it crosses a **platform** or bridge, the distance is (Train Length + Platform Length).

Unit Conversion

To convert **km/hr to m/s**, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert **m/s to km/hr**, multiply the speed by 18/5.</p

questions.question: A car travels at a speed of 80 km/hr and covers a particular distance in 4 hour 30 minutes. How much time (in hours) another car travelling at the speed of 30 km/hr will take to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the **distance** is constant, Speed is inversely proportional to Time (S ∝ 1/T).

Ratio of Speeds = 80 : 30 = 8 : 3

Ratio of Times = 3 : 8

Given, 3 units = 4.5 hr → 1 unit = 1.5 hr

Time for second car = 8 units = 8 × 1.5 = 12 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Speed** of the first car (S₁) = 80 km/hr

**Time** taken by the first car (T₁) = 4 hr 30 min = 4.5 hr

**Speed** of the second car (S₂) = 30 km/hr

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a3ef2560294ca8a8e64aa76fe0970b31c704e649318d5cdf2e329da76d91e5d.png] 

**Formula used:**

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered by first car = 80 × 4.5

⇒ Distance = 360 km

⇒ Time taken by second car = Distance ÷ Speed₂

⇒ Time = 360 ÷ 30

⇒ Time = 12 hr

**∴ The correct answer is 12 hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion in Motion

When distance is **constant**, speed (S) is inversely proportional to time (T). Formula: S₁T₁ = S₂T₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert **minutes to hours**, divide by 60. Example: 30 min = 30/60 = 0.5 hr.

Average Speed for Constant Distance

If an object covers the same distance at speeds x and y, **Average Speed** = (2 × x × y) ÷ (x + y).</p
